title: Console Navigation Framework: Siderail Consolidation & Contextual Workspace Lens
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem statement: As the Console surface has grown (dashboards, rollouts, cost breakdowns, model routes), teams report discovery friction: features are buried in deep rails, workspace switching is noisy, and users accidentally change global state when they intend to scope views. This ticket proposes a new information architecture and navigation framework that reduces cognitive load, clarifies scope, and surfaces high-value console lenses (Dashboards, Rollouts, Cost, Models, Routes) with role-aware affordances.

Goals:
- Consolidate the left rail into a lightweight, collapsible Siderail with persistent workspace context.
- Introduce a contextual Workspace Lens that crops the Console surface to the chosen scope (workspace, project, model, or allocation).
- Surface high-priority lenses (Dashboards, Rollouts, Cost) as first-class navigation entry points with previews and quick actions.
- Preserve fast power-user flows (keyboard quick-switcher, deep links, pinned tabs) while simplifying discoverability for new users.

Constraints and design principles:
- Backwards-compatible deep links and existing routes must continue to work; server-side routing layer will map legacy paths to new lens routes.
- Minimal visual real-estate impact: keep core content width >= 960px for eval dashboards.
- Role-aware options: Platform Admins see capacity/allocations; Devs see runbooks/requests.
- Accessibility: keyboard focus order, ARIA on the Siderail and Lens switcher, and color contrast for badges.

Proposed IA (high-level):
- Left Siderail (collapsed by default) contains: Workspace selector (top), Lenses group (Dashboards, Rollouts, Cost, Models, Routes), Utilities (Metrics, Logs, Settings). Each Lens has a small preview flyout (recent dashboards, active rollouts, cost spike alerts).
- Top breadcrumb shows active Lens > Workspace > Resource. Deep-link canonical URL pattern: /lens/:lensId/workspace/:workspaceId/(optional resource/:id).
- Workspace Lens modal/overlay to temporarily scope the Console without navigating away: useful for cross-workspace comparison and for transient role-based inspections.
- Quick-switcher (Cmd/Ctrl+K) extended to include Lens filtering and ability to pin a Lens to the side for session.

Prototype notes and artifacts:
- Primary prototype (Figma): https://www.figma.com/file/Redwood/console-axiom-navigation-2026 (prototype frame: Lens-Flyout-v2)
- Interactive clickthrough (InVision): https://redwood.invisionapp.com/console-axiom-nav-v2
- PRD summary: https://docs.redwood.ai/confluence/console-ia-2026/summary
- Spike exploration: internal doc with route mapping and migration plan: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/console-ia-spike-mapping

Design reviews and feedback log:
- 2026-03-05: Early scoping review with Product (Rohan Patel) and Eng (Priya Singh) — feedback: need explicit rollbacks for rollouts lens and fast fallback routes for SLO-critical pages.
- 2026-03-08: Accessibility pass with Accessibility Guild (Kofi Mensah) — action: add focus-visible states and update ARIA roles for the lens flyouts.
- 2026-03-10: Usability testing (6 participants, internal) — pattern: users expect cost insights next to query filters; we changed the Cost lens preview to include the top 3 cost drivers.
- 2026-03-12: Engineering review (runtime team) — trade-off: continuous preview data increases read ops; agreed on short-polling + cached preview strategy.

Decisions made:
- Adopt Lens-first routing (/lens/...) to reduce route sprawl and make canonical URLs explicit.
- Siderail collapsed by default on small viewports; expanded by default for >1280px screens.
- Preview flyouts use cached, 10s TTL telemetry and are limited to summary metrics to stay within quota.
- Role-aware lens ordering will be driven by server-side settings for enterprise customers.

Open questions / Trade-offs:
- Should workspace switching be optimistic (local state) or require a navigation round-trip to update server-side context? (Engineering leaning toward server update for auditability; design prefers optimistic for perceived performance.)
- How to handle pinned multi-workspace dashboards in the same tab? (Current proposal: only allow pinning within the active workspace; multi-workspace comparison is a separate modal.)

Acceptance criteria (UX):
- Users can switch Lens and Workspace with no more than 2 clicks from console home.
- Dashboards lens shows preview cards with up-to-date summary (10s staleness max) and a one-click open to the full dashboard.
- Rollouts lens exposes active canaries and a direct rollback CTA in the flyout for users with release permissions.
- Cost lens surfaces top 3 cost drivers and a link to the cost explorer with pre-applied filters for the selected workspace.

Engineering handoff notes:
- Route mapping sheet attached in Drive: column mapping legacy -> new. Engineers: Priya Singh, Omar Haddad. Backend tasks: ensure legacy API params (workspace_id, route) accepted on new Lens endpoints.
- Prototype tokens in Figma: tokens/console/side-rail/axiom-v2

Next steps (short term):
- Finalize route mapping and PRD acceptance (owner: Rohan Patel) — due 2026-03-20.
- Developer spike to measure preview read ops and caching pattern (owner: Priya Singh) — spike complete by 2026-03-18.
- High-fidelity accessibility pass and handoff package to Eng (owner: Maya Chen) — deliverable: Figma spec + component tokens by 2026-03-22.

Metrics to measure success:
- Reduction in mean time to find feature (MTFF) for Dashboards / Rollouts / Cost from 28s -> <12s (baseline via event logs).
- Decrease in accidental global state changes from workspace switch telemetry by 50% in first 6 weeks.
- Adoption: % of active users who use Lens quick-switcher at least once per session > 25% within 8 weeks of rollout.
